standard.title: Participate in planning activities with others
standard.description: participate in activities that involve planning with others, using a range of familiar phrases and modelled structures
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can participate in guided play-based activities using formulaic expressions (AC9LS2C02). They use turn-taking and simple collaborative language. They have not yet planned activities with others, used sequencing language, or allocated tasks in the target language.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students participate in activities that involve planning with others — using turn-taking, task allocation, sequencing, decision-making and collaborative language across a range of familiar contexts.

nodes.label: Turn-taking, task allocation and sequencing language
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use language for managing collaborative processes — turn-taking, allocating tasks and sequencing steps — in shared planning activities.
nodes.minimum_width: Use at least two turn-taking or task allocation expressions and at least one sequencing structure in a collaborative activity.
nodes.typical_width: Use turn-taking and acknowledgement language; follow and give procedural sequences step by step; allocate roles in group tasks; use collaborative decision-making language across planning tasks.
wider: Lead a group through a procedure in the target language — calling each step, checking completion and handing over to the next person
Write and present a simple allocation plan for a class event — specifying who will do what using target language
nodes.hinge_reason: Collaborative process language — turn-taking, task allocation, sequencing — is the structural prerequisite for all planning activity. Students who can only participate in unstructured activity cannot manage the organised joint production tasks this standard targets.

response_modes.reason: Collaborative process language needs to become automatic across varied task conditions — different task types, roles and group sizes. Varied collaborative activity provides the practice context.

success_criteria: Uses at least two turn-taking or task allocation expressions in a collaborative activity
Follows or produces at least one sequenced procedure using step language

nodes.label: Collaborative planning for events and shared outputs
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can collaborate with others to plan and produce a shared output — such as an event, invitation, menu, or presentation — using familiar phrases and modelled structures.
nodes.minimum_width: Contribute at least three target language exchanges to a collaborative planning task that produces a shared output.
nodes.typical_width: Plan and produce collaborative outputs across varied task types — event plans, invitations, menus, scripts, bilingual resources; use language for making choices and decisions; contribute to content, vocabulary and design decisions using familiar vocabulary.
wider: Take a leadership role in a collaborative planning task — initiating decisions, managing contributions and presenting the shared outcome to an audience
Create an invitation or promotional material for a real class event — making deliberate decisions about content, vocabulary and audience

response_modes.reason: Collaborative planning integrates turn-taking and sequencing language (N1) with productive output creation. Tasks with genuine shared stakes — a real event, a real audience — make the integration condition authentic.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Planning for real audiences — a buddy class, a school event — creates genuine communicative stakes that are qualitatively different from classroom simulation.
success_criteria: Contributes at least three target language exchanges to a collaborative planning task
Produces or contributes to a shared output using appropriate target language
